measured_alias_state.note: The lead's plan (deploy-verify-plan2.md 0.4) recorded that alias/aws/ssm had NO backing key. It has one now. It was created 91 seconds before I read it, during this verification pass, with zero SSM parameters in the region - so it was materialised by a read (aws kms list-aliases / describe-key), not by a SecureString write. Reported as measured; I ran no write call.

kms.consequence_for_first_cold_start: the AWS-managed key now exists and is Enabled, so the first GetParameter WithDecryption does not have to wait on key creation. The previous 'no backing key' risk is gone.
kms.consequence_for_encryption_context_condi: kms:EncryptionContext:PARAMETER_ARN is still UNEXERCISED - no SecureString has ever been decrypted on this account. If SSM's context does not match byte-for-byte the cold start fails AccessDeniedException on kms:Decrypt and /v1/health reports dsn_unavailable. The named, one-variable fallback is restrict_kms_to_parameter = false, which keeps kms:ViaService. This is a runtime risk, not an apply risk, and it is reversible.

wrapper_deploy_sh.question: does deploy.sh do anything to the Cloud database around the apply, and is any of it destructive or irreversible
wrapper_deploy_sh.answer: yes, before the apply, and one opt-in path is irreversible
wrapper_deploy_sh.stage_order: 0 preflight, 1 bootstrap_state.sh, 2 ssm put-parameter, 3 cloud_chain.py + seed_demo.py, 4 build zip, 5 optional site upload, 6 terraform init/plan/apply, 7 https proof, 8 demo_acceptance.py, 9 hand-off

the_gate_gates_only_stage_6.fact: without MAINLINE_APPLY_APPROVED=1 the script exits 7 AFTER stages 1-5 have run. So a 'plan-only' deploy has already created the state bucket, written the DSN SecureString, applied migrations to the Cloud database and seeded it. Only --dry-run and --preflight-only write nothing at all.

findings.title: teardown's verify has four blind spots
findings.detail: the verify block (teardown.sh:602-626) re-reads buckets, the SSM parameter and Lambda functions. It never re-reads the IAM role mainline-demo-api-exec, the log group /aws/lambda/mainline-demo-api, the four alarms or the dashboard. If terraform destroy is skipped (teardown.sh:332 skips step 1 whenever the state bucket is already gone) those six resources are orphaned and teardown still exits 0 saying 'nothing this project created remains'.
findings.cost_of_the_orphans: USD 0.00 - an IAM role is free, an empty log group is free, 4 alarms are inside the free 10 and 1 dashboard inside the free 3
findings.fix: add three read-only checks to the verify block: iam list-roles filtered on ${NAME_PREFIX}, logs describe-log-groups --log-group-name-prefix /aws/lambda/${NAME_PREFIX}, cloudwatch describe-alarms --alarm-name-prefix ${NAME_PREFIX}

findings.title: the bucket tag check is a substring match over the whole tag document
findings.detail: teardown.sh:239 is grep -q '"Value": *"mainline"' over the JSON of ALL tags, so a bucket with any tag whose value is exactly mainline passes, not only project=mainline
findings.why_it_is_low: unreachable except for a bucket that already carries the mainline-demo- prefix, and no such bucket exists in this account
findings.fix: match the pair, e.g. python -c on the JSON asserting TagSet contains {Key: project, Value: mainline}

findings.title: the state bucket has no bucket policy
findings.detail: bootstrap_state.sh sets versioning, all four public-access blocks, SSE-S3, tags and a lifecycle rule, but never calls put-bucket-policy. There is no Deny on aws:SecureTransport=false and no principal allowlist.
findings.why_it_is_low: the state object holds no secret, the public-access block already excludes anonymous readers, and cross-account access is impossible without a policy
findings.fix: one put-bucket-policy with a single Deny on aws:SecureTransport false, after the public-access-block call

findings.title: the approval gate does not gate the secret write or the database migration
findings.detail: deploy.sh reaches the gate only after stages 1-5, so a run without MAINLINE_APPLY_APPROVED has already created the state bucket, written the SecureString and migrated + seeded the Cloud database. The script's own gate text says so ('Stages 1 to 5 have already run'), but the RUNBOOK framing of 'plan-only deploy' invites the opposite reading.
findings.fix: none required for the apply; worth one sentence in docs/deploy/RUNBOOK.md

findings.title: infra/modules/demo-api/README.md:129 shows /mainline/demo/dsn, the deployed name is /mainline/demo/cockroach_dsn
findings.detail: a copy-paste example in the module README names a different parameter than deploy.sh:157, teardown.sh:84, terraform.tfvars.example:53 and the plan all use. Nothing executes the README, and deploy.sh:484-489 asserts the real agreement at preflight, so it cannot cause a wrong deploy - only a wrong hand-fix.

findings.title: the lead's 'alias/aws/ssm has no backing key' is no longer true
findings.detail: measured at 2026-08-12T12:47:39Z: the alias targets AWS-managed key 81edadd5-dfa0-428b-a3c6-7694a7917577, Enabled, created 2026-08-12T12:46:08Z, with zero SSM parameters in the region. It was materialised by a read during this pass. The first-cold-start concern the lead raised is resolved; the kms:EncryptionContext:PARAMETER_ARN condition remains unexercised.

verdict.scope: W3's slice only - the DSN path, public-repo exposure, the state backend, blast radius and rollback
verdict.reason: the DSN reaches the Lambda only as a KMS-encrypted SecureString read at runtime and cached per execution environment; it appears in no plan, no state, no log, no committed file and in none of the 53 commits; the plan is 11 creates that address nothing pre-existing in a region that holds nothing; and destroy+teardown is bounded by a prefix-plus-live-tag filter that provably cannot reach the seven unrelated buckets or the one unrelated distribution
verdict.not_in_scope: the reserved_concurrent_executions = 20 vs an account ceiling of 10 (W4/W5) and the unauthenticated mutating routes (W2). Either can still make the aggregate a NO-GO.
verdict.conditions: none blocking. W3-F1 is the one fix worth making before anyone relies on teardown's exit code.
